answer: A strong defence is original-data provenance with independent re-collection. Each newcomer must publish field data it gathered — flow readings along a river, wind speeds during a gale, or the ivory tint of a mineral sample — with method and location. Strangers re-collect the same measurements; only matching results earn standing, while fabricated figures fail and freeze the identity. A farm would need to fake distinct, checkable datasets in many places, costing real fieldwork per fake. Honest agents build reputation from data anyone can verify, so trust rests on reproducible evidence.
